interventions.name: Direct-to-chip cooling, with site-selected dry heat rejection and control optimization
interventions.relevant_activity: Operating owned or cooperatively managed leased datacenters; eligible refresh of existing compute service.
interventions.maturity_evidence: Vertiv commercial direct-to-chip CDU product family available in EMEA June 2025; Microsoft deployment and operational disclosures. Integrated Microsoft zero-evaporation new-build design has deployment timing uncertainty; components are available, not proof every legacy site is retrofit-ready.
baseline_inputs_needed: Equivalent delivered virtual-core-hours, memory/storage and SLA, separately from AI accelerator service
Eligible air-cooled rack/server inventory, refresh schedule and compatibility
Site hourly IT and total electricity, cooling water withdrawal/consumption, weather and heat rejection design
Site marginal power/water factors and coolant/refrigerant inventory

quantified_effects.unit: relative cradle-to-grave kgCO2e per annualized virtual core
quantified_effects.case: Cold plate vs air, 2021 US average-grid model

quantified_effects.unit: relative MJ per annualized virtual core
quantified_effects.case: Same model; NOT metered electricity savings

quantified_effects.unit: relative life-cycle water per annualized virtual core
quantified_effects.case: Same model; NOT site-only water withdrawals
Only for cooling evaporation eliminated by a fully dry closed-loop design; excludes fill, maintenance, sanitation, upstream electricity and manufacturing

interventions.applicability_bounds: LCA assumes 15-year datacenter, 6-year servers; cold-plate scenario has 20% overclocking, 28% more virtual cores and 3% lower PUE. Cannot infer generic fleet or AI GPU reduction. Baseline service must actually be deliverable with this configuration. Water-free heat rejection is a different design comparison and may increase power.

bounded_subcase.interpretation: 0–981 ML is only a deliberately loose gross withdrawal ceiling at fixed FY25 service/weather, not a deployment estimate, net lifecycle saving, or expected range. Actual cooling fraction, necessary withdrawals and feasible retrofit share are unknown.

interventions.conditional_calculation: For independently validated LCA-matched cohort: avoided GHG = 0.15 * cohort baseline cradle-to-grave GHG; avoided blue water = 0.31 * matched cohort baseline lifecycle consumption. For dry conversion: avoided site water = eligible cooling evaporation eliminated, then subtract additional upstream water. Do not combine these as independent savings.

uptake_by_2031.scenario: Replace only eligible racks at documented scheduled refreshes through 2031; dry conversion only after site engineering and power/water tradeoff measurement. No public cohort inventory supports a percentage.

interventions.already_implemented_or_committed: New designs use zero-evaporation approach since August 2024; published schedule says pilots in 2026/new sites online late 2027. June 2026 disclosure says about 90% of owned fleet already uses efficient low-/zero-water cooling and Phoenix WUE improved 23% in FY25, with operational improvements rolling out globally.

costs.cashflow_formula: Avoided purchased kWh * tariff + avoided billed water/sewer * tariff - added electricity - service/maintenance - financing/admin. Use measured electricity, not primary-energy LCA percentage.
costs.warning: Water-driven dry conversion can worsen electricity operating cost; no quoted Microsoft retrofit cost or payback found.

interventions.repayable_mechanism: Proposed equipment lease or metered savings contract; fund finances compatible cooling equipment and receives actual contracted payments. Only underwrite measured, creditworthy cashflow sufficient for nominal principal plus losses and administration; not a water-damage valuation.
interventions.additional_investor_effect: Unproven. Exclude existing installed or funded/committed work; identify a financing-constrained eligible retrofit and demonstrate acceleration or otherwise absent deployment.
constraints_and_shifted_harms: Electrical capacity/headroom, uptime and shutdown windows, liquid compatibility, warranties, chip service equivalence
Dry rejection adds electricity and possibly upstream water/emissions; site climate matters
Coolant/refrigerant manufacture, leakage, disposal and copper replacement; use product-specific inventory
Two-phase immersion excluded from selected intervention; its fluid hazards and architecture differ
overlap: Electricity decarbonization reduces the carbon benefit of electricity efficiency; calculate once on residual electricity
Do not add dry cooling, controls and the full cold-plate LCA percentage for same cohort
Construction embodied impacts already included in LCA must not be counted again under timber

interventions.name: Hybrid cross-laminated timber structure for eligible replacement datacenter buildings
interventions.relevant_activity: Embodied construction emissions in capital goods; only construction required to sustain fixed service output fits strict fixed-output case.
interventions.maturity_evidence: Commercial CLT; Microsoft had a CLT campus in 2021 and reported its first two hybrid datacenters built in May 2025.
baseline_inputs_needed: Project-specific same-capacity steel or precast design BOM and embodied LCA
Eligible replacement building area/volume through 2031, excluding growth-only capacity
CLT procurement, sourcing/forest counterfactual, product EPD, transport and end-of-life treatment

quantified_effects.status: Microsoft two-project estimate, not measured fleet-wide factor
Alternative baseline, not additive to steel comparison

interventions.applicability_bounds: Apply only to a project with the same structural/service requirements and comparable LCA boundary. Public announcement does not expose module boundaries, absolute emissions or biogenic accounting. Cannot apply to total Scope 3 capital goods (which also contains servers and equipment).
interventions.conditional_calculation: Avoided project embodied emissions = 0.35 * independently validated comparable steel-building baseline, OR 0.65 * comparable precast baseline. Sum only verified eligible replacement projects; do not sum the two factors.

bounded_subcase.interpretation: Unit scenario only; not evidence that Microsoft has an unimplemented one-tonne or larger eligible cohort.

uptake_by_2031.scenario: Eligible naturally required replacements with completed structural/fire approvals and contracted material supply. If no building replacement needed to sustain baseline output by 2031, strict fixed-output construction subcase is zero; do not invent growth projects to create savings.

interventions.already_implemented_or_committed: Two Virginia hybrid buildings and campus timber are existing actions. Low-carbon material procurement is already an active program.

costs.warning: Published 5–10% premium compares CLT with traditional residential timber, not datacenter steel/concrete; unusable as project premium. Need comparable contractor bids.
costs.possible_cash_benefit: Shorter construction or lower steel quantities could reduce total project cost, but unquantified.

interventions.repayable_mechanism: Proposed supplier equipment/working-capital loan secured by purchase orders, or eligible property lease. Repayment comes from timber sales or lease payments. A material price premium alone has no automatic savings stream.
interventions.additional_investor_effect: Requires supplier capacity or working-capital bottleneck and additional uncommitted eligible orders; buying Microsoft shares or refinancing existing construction does not establish extra avoided emissions.
constraints_and_shifted_harms: Fire/structural code, moisture, loads, local construction skills and transport
Forest harvest counterfactual, biodiversity, land competition, adhesives and end-of-life carbon release must be evaluated
Construction-only result is not annual recurring reduction unless lifecycle annualization is explicitly adopted
overlap: Other low-carbon concrete/steel strategies act on remaining material quantities; never stack whole-building percentages
Recalculate building component if combined with cold-plate whole-datacenter LCA

interventions.name: Additional wind/solar supply with storage or existing hydro flexibility where deliverable
interventions.relevant_activity: Datacenter electricity, focusing on residual fossil generation serving fixed existing service demand.
interventions.maturity_evidence: Operating renewable portfolio and Powerex hourly-matched hydro/wind/solar service demonstrate commercial procurement models; regional replication remains contingent on physical resources.
baseline_inputs_needed: Hourly location-specific loads, grid dispatch/marginal emissions, existing contracted generators and start dates
Generation profiles, connection status, transmission rights, curtailment and storage roundtrip losses
Generation and storage lifecycle EPDs, land/water/ecology data
Incremental capex, PPA price, maintenance, tax, debt seniority and repayment schedule

quantified_effects.reason: No Microsoft/site-specific credible marginal displacement factor established; annual certificates or grid-average inventory differences are insufficient.

quantified_effects.unit: direct combustion CO2 from wind/solar operation
quantified_effects.reason: Physical non-combustion generation property; excludes full lifecycle and grid counterfactual. Never use as zero lifecycle emissions.

interventions.conditional_calculation: Avoided physical tCO2e = sum_hour(additional delivered MWh * displaced marginal tCO2e/MWh) - incremental lifecycle generation/storage/grid emissions - induced system leakage. Must model project system counterfactual; storage shifts time and loses energy, it does not itself generate clean power.

uptake_by_2031.scenario: Only new incremental, permitted/interconnected projects feasibly operating by 2031 and demonstrably serving/displacing residual fossil energy. Existing contracted projects belong in no-new-fund case.

interventions.already_implemented_or_committed: February 2026: 40 GW renewable supply contracted, 19 GW online, remainder expected over five years; FY25 annual renewable matching achieved. Powerex agreement provides hourly service in Washington. These are not unclaimed future funding benefits.

costs.cashflow_formula: Actual project PPA/electricity receipts minus O&M, taxes, lease, replacement reserve and senior debt; compare contractual repayable cash to fund principal.
costs.warning: No Microsoft-specific contract prices/project costs retrieved; generic LCOE is not a PPA price or guaranteed investment return.

interventions.repayable_mechanism: Proposed project loan to additional contracted wind/solar/storage assets, repaid from PPA receipts. A Microsoft offtake can support bankability, but availability of such investment and principal recovery require diligence; neither is established here.
interventions.additional_investor_effect: Demonstrate fund causes financing close, earlier in-service date or additional project volume beyond 40 GW commitments and business-as-usual developers. PPA additionality is not identical to this fund additionality.
constraints_and_shifted_harms: Interconnection/transmission, seasonal mismatch, firm capacity and storage losses
Land/biodiversity, mining/material processing and disposal; hydro water/ecological impacts
Reallocating existing clean electricity can leave other customers with more fossil power; hourly matching alone does not resolve counterfactual
overlap: Apply to electricity remaining after efficiency; do not add market/location Scope2 accounting gap as avoided physical emissions
Supplier clean electricity and Microsoft direct electricity must be attributed separately to avoid double counting
